CH2008-WIN.evidence: Chase et al. Table 1 and sections 2–4. Correlated offset drives show an 86 cm package in a 3.9 m deep cirque lake with shore-side avalanche tracks. Stratigraphic attribution and good local recovery do not quantify upslope or underwater focusing.

CH2008-THU.evidence: Chase et al. Table 1 and section 4.2. The two contacts enclose 32 cm in gyttja. Authors describe poor correlation of parallel drives above the marker in this 2.9 m deep lake.

M2024-ROUNDWA.evidence: Mark thesis section 5.3.1, Fig. 46. The approximately 606–666 cm event package lies within carbonate-rich sediment. No quantified primary fraction, catchment input or focusing correction supports a minimum of 60 cm.

B2020-113.evidence: Buckland S1 row 125 reports two layers. Mehringer in Johnson et al. (1994) p. 6 and his Columbia River Basin account describe two horizons separated by 9 cm of lake sediment. The 46 cm cannot be assigned to one climactic bed, or shown to enclose the complete deposit of that eruption.

B2020-073.evidence: Buckland et al. report 30 cm of continuous fine tephra over a sharp contact below developed soil at Andies Prairie. Their field visit and S2 watershed-divide analysis support their explicit minimum interpretation.

B2020-038.evidence: S1 gives 68 cm as an upland thickness. The original field log, scope of phases and physical basis of the upland value could not be independently tied to this exposure. Young’s separately numbered mapped sections retain their own evidence.

B2020-049.evidence: Buckland S1 gives 37 cm. The four-lake study abstract does not identify this value by lake, and the recovered investigator archive entry is a modern surface sample. Neither verifies complete recovery of this tephra at the nominated site.

B2020-059.evidence: The investigator archive identifies the Mazama depth control but quotes a 1 cm dating sample and a different depth from S1. The 17 cm S1 value cannot be aligned to a confirmed original bed and bounded recovery.

B2020-177.evidence: S1 gives a varying 15 cm for the Maple Leaf site. Jensen et al. Table S1 reports a 15 cm observation at Stampede (UA 2825), a separate site, and contains no entry for Maple Leaf. The original excavation profile assigning 15 cm to one intact blanket is unresolved.

B2020-149.evidence: The Mack study and the corrected Tepee Lake location support an occurrence. Neither the accessible original account nor Kuehn’s separate Glacier Peak sample establishes a 10 cm climactic bed, its contacts or retention.

B2020-121.evidence: S1 reports 5 cm at Creston/Wilbur Bog. Its relation to Creston Bog (S1 120) and to differently reported corrected and uncorrected values is unresolved. An exact section and original preserved bed were not identified.

B2020-227.evidence: Hallett et al. dated charcoal within the Dog Lake ash. The 10 cm compilation value and the 23 cm Dog Lake unit cited by Jensen Table S1 row 62 cannot presently be assigned to one particular core and transfer. Both readings remain in the ledger.

B2020-042.evidence: Table S2 places ash at 102 cm between wood samples at 75.5 and 130 cm. The enclosing 54.5 cm is a gross ceiling under full capture. The older age of reworked wood at 130 cm invalidates that radiocarbon tie for the age model; its physical depth is documented. S1’s 1 cm is retained separately as a compilation reading.

B2020-122.evidence: The historical wet 15–30 cm at Newman Lake and the 22.5 cm compilation midpoint do not locate both endpoints at a single recoverable core footprint or control lake focusing. Either gain or loss is possible; neither endpoint supplies a defensible sign.

B2020-017.evidence: Bovet et al. confirm coring and the ash/date marker, and S1 describes the recovered package as 2–6 cm. Use the largest reported bed to allow local focusing, conditional on the compiled range applying to this lake and on complete capture.

B2020-019.evidence: Bovet et al. identify a cored eastern subbasin after abandoning the deep basin. The S1 2–6 cm range is not an independent field measurement. The 6 cm upper endpoint allows focusing under the qualified core and retention assignment.

B2020-063.evidence: Young Table 1.1 and Fig. 1.14 identify a field-checked bog locality and standardize the loading to 700 kg/m³. Halving the standardized thickness accounts for a proposed bulk-density ratio but does not bound lateral import, wet-to-dry volume change or older ash. Observer values and Young’s estimate remain a common alternative.

B2020-068.evidence: Young Table 1.1 and Fig. 1.14 identify a field-checked bog locality and standardize the loading to 700 kg/m³. Halving the standardized thickness accounts for a proposed bulk-density ratio but does not bound lateral import, wet-to-dry volume change or older ash. Observer values and Young’s estimate remain a common alternative.

B2020-076.evidence: Young Table 1.1 and Fig. 1.14 identify a field-checked bog locality and standardize the loading to 700 kg/m³. Halving the standardized thickness accounts for a proposed bulk-density ratio but does not bound lateral import, wet-to-dry volume change or older ash. Observer values and Young’s estimate remain a common alternative.

B2020-023.evidence: The 5 cm tephra V is independently measured and compositionally distinguished from tephra VI. The investigators specifically discuss rapid settling and possible subaqueous flow in connection with its unusual magnetic direction. The logged deposit may exceed local fallout.

B2020-099.evidence: The Buckland extraction gives both contacts, 7.21–7.27 m, and the independent dating crosswalk brackets Mazama at Davis Lake. The 6 cm is a recovered-host ceiling conditional on the inherited depths and continuity; it is not a separately verified primary blanket measurement.

B2020-126.evidence: The investigator’s report differentiates a near-margin debris-flow occurrence from other Leland cores, and verifies Mazama by microprobe. The section at which the compiled 2 cm was measured has not been matched to its geochemistry and depositional state.

B2020-174.evidence: The Squeah nearshore core has correlated ash and an underlying radiocarbon sample (I-5347). The site-specific source thickness and completeness of the S1 2 cm package at this position remain unresolved.

B2020-160.evidence: Several Lulu Island holes and X-ray emission analyses support eruption identity. The compilation does not identify the exact borehole and contacts associated with 1.5 cm or whether it is a whole bed.

B2020-148.evidence: S1 explicitly distinguishes an 8 cm earlier fall and 12 cm climactic unit. Valastro et al. establish two intervals in the fen. A 12 cm ceiling allows concentration in the later peat bed; it is conditional on the source assigning that complete reported unit to this hole.

B2020-291.evidence: The historic corer recorded a 1 mm layer and Young Table 1.1 gives an upper equivalent of 0.2 cm at 700 kg/m³. Jensen S1 row 57 corroborates that an identifiable visible Mazama horizon was reported. Use Young’s stated ceiling, conditional on the density and source recovery; no calibrated zero or detection threshold.

M2014-CLELAND-F.evidence: Mihindukulasooriya’s F-09 ash interval is 4 or 5 cm in the primary accounts. Use the larger complete-bed endpoint to allow concentration. Carbonate-rich material in the different E-09 core cannot independently measure primary thickness at F-09.

W1995-TT06313.evidence: The original workshop account reports an identified discrete offshore ash at 209–211 cm. Whether those limits are whole physical contacts or the sampled slice cannot be resolved. Sea-floor transport and export can change the loading in either direction.

ROS2004-EAG.evidence: Rosenberg et al. Tables 2 and 4 support the eruption identity, including glass chemistry, and a 15 cm core package (81–96 cm). Central-basin accumulation is not independently compared with a local atmospheric blanket.

ROS2004-FRO.evidence: Rosenberg et al. Table 2 separates the 155–163 cm lake package from other units. Its full 8 cm supports a conditional retention ceiling. No independently separated primary thickness is reported.

P1999-BEAVER-OR.evidence: The thesis and published chronology place the complete 2 cm Beaver Lake interval at different composite depths. A common 2 cm package in the lake can allow lateral addition without imposing a positive original minimum.

MK2012-PATJENS.evidence: McKay describes a 4 cm silicic bed in a short south-shore fen core. The correlation is presumed from stratigraphy and grain size. The whole bed could have been augmented in this setting.

W2017-LSUNRISE.evidence: Coring ended within the tephra after 3 cm. It is a firm lower limit on recovered lake material. The missing lower contact prevents a full-package ceiling, and the investigators do not calibrate focusing at the coring position.

R2021-LONG.evidence: Rushton et al. report approximately 7 cm in the LOL14C eastern Cascades composite. Composite-depth and chronology discrepancies and unquantified focusing weaken a point reading; the entire package gives a conditional ceiling.

B2020-203.evidence: Mathewes describes a discrete 3.5 cm glass-bearing layer with stratigraphic age support at Surprise Lake. Only the complete lake bed is measured; use a retention-conditional ceiling.

B2020-251.evidence: Mathewes describes 5 cm in Marion Lake. The deep coring position and rapid flushing leave focusing unresolved. Interpret the complete bed as a retention-conditional ceiling.

B2020-205.evidence: Lowdon and Blake GSC-1004 describe a 10 cm peat-contained ash and query the Mazama assignment. The complete logged bed allows a conditional ceiling if the correlation holds.

B2020-169.evidence: Lowdon and Blake GSC-875 separate an 8 cm lower peat bed from a 3 cm upper ash. The climactic correlation of the lower bed is taken from later work. Compression and archives of imported ash remain uncertain.

MAR2009-S15.evidence: Marcott’s creek section places tephra immediately over till and below sand. The mapped 50–66 cm recovered thickness is an outward interval read from the section; fluvial or glacial concentration cannot be excluded at this position. Keep the upper endpoint under full retention.

MAR2009-S05.evidence: The upstream cutbank contains separated ash-bearing bands and outwash. The 4–9 cm graphical estimate for one band neither isolates an unaffected primary basal fallout layer nor encloses all possible target material.

B2020-275.evidence: Jensen et al. Table S1 row 27, UA 2901. The fresh road-cut section has a sharp base and a reworked top; the whole layer varies from 2 to 5 cm. Use 5 cm as a conditional ceiling at the reported field coordinate. The 2–3 cm typical thickness contains an unresolved secondary share.

B2020-285.evidence: Jensen et al. Table S1 row 50, UA 2979, reports a questioned upper thickness of 1 cm in Hasse Lake, with glass analyzed. The 253–266 cm field entry is a core-depth range. S1 warns of distortion. Accept the author’s tentative upper only if recovery is complete.

R2001-KSNEA.evidence: Riedel, Pringle and Schuster separate an abrupt 2 cm basal airfall above pre-eruption lake sediment from as much as 17 m of reworked delta. Pringle and Scott corroborate this measured component as co-author testimony. The point represents the delta near the creek mouth.

L2012-ROE.evidence: Fig. 2 resolves the ash between 573.0 and 573.5 cm. The photographed discrete layer, composition and depositional setting support a 0.5 cm preserved primary bed.

L2016-STOWELL.evidence: Lemmen logs a 2 cm bed at 330.5–332.5 cm in organic sediment. Stratigraphic age and regional chemistry comparisons support a likely Mazama attribution.

M2013-NEL01.evidence: Six centimetres in one lacustrine core. The original author correlates the bed to the climactic eruption using the stratigraphic age model.

M2013-NEL03.evidence: Tables 2.2 and 3.1 imply 27 and 26 cm for the lower airfall bed. The separate upper redeposit is 6.5–8.5 cm and contains weathered clay. The small basin has an inlet; take the wider primary package as a conditional ceiling.

M2012-ONOFF02.evidence: Fig. 5, PDF p. 6 (printed p. 76), core 02. Continuous Unit 2 encloses the 141 cm glass signal. Axis ticks 0/150 cm at y=202/563; outward contact picks 405/601 pixels at 1042×1389 yield 81.44 cm rounded outward to 82. The whole host unit is deliberately broad.

N2004-CASTOR.evidence: Nelson describes rapid deposition of about 30 cm of ash and later continuing surface wash. Only the initial package supplies an approximate conditional upper bound.

E1997-A12.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core A12. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=135–606 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=513–520 span 3.57 cm, rounded upward to 4 cm. Section L3/L4 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.

E1997-B7B.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core B7b. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=135–616 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=233–273 span 19.96 cm, rounded upward to 20 cm. Section P2/P3 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.

E1997-C5.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core C5. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=138–622 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=412–438 span 12.89 cm, rounded upward to 13 cm. Section G3/G4 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.

E1997-D8.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core D8. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=143–625 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=338–394 span 27.88 cm, rounded upward to 28 cm. Section Q2/Q3 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.

B2020-047.evidence: Long et al. (2011) measured a distinct 50 cm package at 4.84–5.34 m in the Tumalo core and assigned it by chronology. Local sediment focusing and retention were not calibrated. The original 50 cm observation is preserved.

B2020-054.evidence: McKay (2012), §3.4.3.4 and Fig. 3.8. A 14 cm silicic bed from 267–281 cm was attributed by grain size and stratigraphy. Other mafic layers are distinct. Sediment delivery at this Round Lake, Oregon, is uncalibrated.

W2017-SHADOW.evidence: Walsh et al. (2017), Table 2 and §4.1. Shadow Lake SL11C has a separate 14 cm Mazama-O layer, identified visually by J. Vallance with stratigraphic/age control. Deep coring reduces marginal disturbance; deposition per unit lakefloor area remains uncalibrated.

W2017-SUNRISE.evidence: Walsh et al. (2017), Table 2 and §4.2. At Sunrise Lake UL11D the 8 cm Mazama-O layer is distinct from younger and older tephras. Deep coring and cross-lake occurrence support the bed correlation. Catchment capture and redistribution can alter the local thickness.

S2023-DOG-OR.evidence: Saban (2023), pp. 66 and 76. An abrupt-contact package at 908–920 cm has multiple subcentimetre layers; the chronology uses 13 cm. The earlier 928–927 cm bed is separate. Use the larger 13 cm description if the complete local fall is retained.

S2023-WHITEPINE.evidence: Saban (2023), Table 3 and pp. 95–103, 110–113. The marsh bed contains 1–2 mm lapilli with basal fine ash, which supports eruptive deposition. Reported package equivalents are 25, 26.5 and approximately 30 cm. Local fallout cannot be bounded below without ruling out concentration in the shallow basin.

L2024-JEN13-2E.evidence: The source-labelled 2016 Fig. 3a photo is independently matched to 2024 Fig. S3, JEN13-2, first section. Outer contact picks y=402–709 enclose the diffuse ash; ruler 0–10 cm is y=15–831 in the original 1028×1298 image. The 3.76 cm outer package rounds upward to 4 cm. The point sample at 93.5 cm and 17 analyses establish identity.

L2024-JEN15-3A.evidence: Fig. 3 places the marker between two independently drawn turbidite contacts. The outward 313–372 pixel interval at x=520 converts to 62.60 cm then ≤63 cm using the 0–800 cm scale y=190–944 (920×1300 rendering). Table S2 independently encloses it at 132.25–204 cm. The tephra symbol is conventionally enlarged.

L2024-JEN16-1A.evidence: Table S3 reports the base of the younger 5.3 ka turbidite at 184 cm and the top of the older 7.7 ka turbidite at 232 cm in this drive. Table S2 places Mazama at 230.5 cm. The host between them spans 48 cm. Overlapping B and 2021 cores repeat the horizon.

L2024-JEN16-2.evidence: The intervening unit lies between a separate sand horizon and the top of an older turbidite. Outward contacts y=475–525, x=234, on the 920×1300 Fig. 3 rendering give 53.05 cm and round upward to ≤54 cm (0–800 cm at y=190–944). Table S2 places the marker at 350 cm. Inflow and bottom transport are especially important at this site.

B2020-217.evidence: Figure 5.2 and p. 43 give 94–96 cm in the original core. The compilation lists 10 cm; a 2 cm envelope applies specifically to UKANL1.

B2020-245.evidence: Pages 68–71 distinguish initial fall from later slopewash incorporated in the 28 cm unit, with abundant charcoal, seeds and sediment. The 10 cm compilation value is unverified for another section.

B2020-250.evidence: Pages 58–61 and Figs. 5.8–5.9 show 108 cm of charcoal-rich ash at 124–232 cm, followed by ash-bearing peaty slopewash to 280 cm. The author identifies secondary accumulation. 280 minus 124 gives a broad 156 cm containment ceiling if the original local fall was fully retained. Neither 100 nor 108 measures primary airfall.

B2020-211.evidence: Pages 72–76, Figs. 5.15–5.16. Dispersed ash through 10 cm of peat immediately above a wind- or wave-cut unconformity. Erosion and exposure prevent a credible upper or lower bound on the original local fall.

B1997-COPL1.evidence: Beierle logs a distinct 1 cm bed at 259–260 cm. The surviving package limits fallout only if retention is complete. An independent field campaign at the same lake cannot certify the thickness of a compilation row.

B1997-LL1.evidence: Beierle logs a distinct 7 cm bed at 521–528 cm. The surviving package limits fallout only if retention is complete. An independent field campaign at the same lake cannot certify the thickness of a compilation row.

B1997-LBSL2.evidence: Gyttja below and above encloses a 5 cm layer at marks 68–73. In-basin redistribution is unquantified.

B1997-SUML1.evidence: Mazama rests on gyttja at mark 387 cm above the base. Sediment overlying the ash was seen before it was lost during splitting. Whole pre-splitting recovery of 530 cm gives at most 143 cm between that contact and the top. Figure 5.11 clips the ash at the plot border. No measured upper ash contact survives.

B1997-SIBL1.evidence: The 50 cm ash-rich interval is unusually thick. Beierle attributes excess to slopewash associated with drought and/or fire. Original local fallout could be substantially thinner.

B2020-132.evidence: Gowan Fig. 2.4 and ch. 2 place the complete marker at 137 cm inside the retained gyttja between 0 and 313 cm. The full enclosing unit supports at most 313 cm. Uniform graphic symbols and core depth are not thickness measurements.

B2020-137.evidence: Gowan Fig. 2.4 and ch. 2 place the complete marker at 158 cm inside the retained gyttja between 74 and 201 cm. The full enclosing unit supports at most 127 cm. Uniform graphic symbols and core depth are not thickness measurements.

B2020-138.evidence: Gowan Fig. 2.4 and ch. 2 place the complete marker at 201 cm inside the retained gyttja between 0 and 329 cm. The full enclosing unit supports at most 329 cm. Uniform graphic symbols and core depth are not thickness measurements.

B2020-140.evidence: Gowan Fig. 2.4 and ch. 2 place the complete marker at 158 cm inside the retained gyttja between 50 and 294 cm. The full enclosing unit supports at most 244 cm. Uniform graphic symbols and core depth are not thickness measurements.

H2026-FROG.evidence: The author physically collected contiguous early and late Holocene charcoal intervals. Their inner ends at 180 and 405 cm enclose the 395 cm tephra marker and give a gross ≤225 cm section. The Neotoma raw charcoal series starts its older block at 405.5 cm. The chronology program removed ash thickness; its anchor width and Fig. 2 line give no physical bed measurement.
H2026-FROG.assumption: The two physical sampling blocks are on the common native composite scale and span the bed; full local fallout survives within that span. Age-model depth offsets, erosion, loss or compaction could invalidate the ceiling.

H2026-SWANSON.evidence: The author physically collected contiguous early and late Holocene charcoal intervals. Their inner ends at 112 and 380 cm enclose the 366 cm tephra marker and give a gross ≤268 cm section. The Neotoma raw charcoal series starts its older block at 380.5 cm. The chronology program removed ash thickness; its anchor width and Fig. 2 line give no physical bed measurement. The archive locates the tie at 366.5 cm.
H2026-SWANSON.assumption: The two physical sampling blocks are on the common native composite scale and span the bed; full local fallout survives within that span. Age-model depth offsets, erosion, loss or compaction could invalidate the ceiling.

H2026-WORLEY.evidence: The author physically collected contiguous early and late Holocene charcoal intervals. Their inner ends at 60 and 250 cm enclose the 241 cm tephra marker and give a gross ≤190 cm section. The Neotoma raw charcoal series starts its older block at 250.5 cm. The chronology program removed ash thickness; its anchor width and Fig. 2 line give no physical bed measurement.
H2026-WORLEY.assumption: The two physical sampling blocks are on the common native composite scale and span the bed; full local fallout survives within that span. Age-model depth offsets, erosion, loss or compaction could invalidate the ceiling.

B2019-BEGBIE.evidence: Brown et al. report both contacts at 405–406 cm in a 633 cm gyttja core. Horrelt reused that same core, with a 406 cm age tie. The preserved bed is 1 cm; later chronology is not a second observation.

H1999-KILPOOLA-1.evidence: Original core 1 records ash at 290–304 cm, a 14 cm preserved package. Two campaigns in the same small lake yield 14 and 33 cm. The deeper 1996 station is registered for the principal analysis; independent exact station coordinates were not published.
H1999-KILPOOLA-1.scope: second core sharing unresolved location; 14 cm alternative

H1999-KILPOOLA-2.evidence: Original core 2 records ash at 470–503 cm, a 33 cm preserved package. Two campaigns in the same small lake yield 14 and 33 cm. The deeper 1996 station is registered for the principal analysis; independent exact station coordinates were not published.

S2009-FOY-A.evidence: Fig. 7c, core A drive 4, pictures a continuous 20–40 cm drive interval. Dashed contacts at roughly 6.6 and 13.5 cm on the 0–20 cm image scale enclose about 7 cm. An outward-rounded 8 cm cap allows contact and scale reading and assumes full retention. The core dried before imaging; shrinkage is uncalibrated.

S2009-FOY-C.evidence: The paper identifies the bed in core C but photographs core A. Pollen samples at 129–130 and 237–238 cm limit the enclosing physical section to ≤109 cm. Inconsistent radiocarbon ages complicate local chronology. Measure the unit in A only at its own station.

B2020-175.evidence: Field notes report more than 100 cm of ash; coring could not penetrate below it. The 1 cm date control is a sample. Neither a whole-bed ceiling nor a local primary minimum is identifiable in this basin. The S1 252 cm is unresolved.
B2020-175.scope: incomplete recovery or absence of registered primary thickness

B2020-176.evidence: The investigator records the Mazama age tie at 221 cm; a zero-width chronology tie supplies no bed thickness. The last dated shallower plant sample is 202.25 cm; an enclosing lower physical contact is unestablished. The archived macrocharcoal profile from the same unit ends at 203.25 cm, shallower than the 221 cm tephra tie.
B2020-176.scope: incomplete recovery or absence of registered primary thickness

B2020-106.evidence: Mehringer’s Fig. 15 shows a distinct Mazama band near 7.7–8.1 m in a fen with recurrent fire-related slopewash. On the 1120-pixel print the 6.5 and 10.5 m ticks are at y=171 and 686; the outside edges at 324 and 378 imply ≤42 cm after outward rounding. The original pollen archive samples 770 and 810.5 cm on either side, and the 771 cm age tie corroborates the horizon. The compiler’s 39 cm is compatible with the recovered bed; original dry-land fallout may have been substantially thinner.

H1976-ELK.evidence: A 10 cm white bed is traceable in a backwater sequence on the east Elk River terrace; the original author tentatively identifies Mazama. Imported sediment, local focusing and possible loss are uncalibrated.

G1988-GOL.evidence: The winter 1981 GOL core retained 575 cm with separate St. Helens Y and Mazama. Without printed contacts the entire measured core supplies only a very loose upper envelope. Old carbon compromises age interpolation. The similarly named fen is separate.

G1989-MICA.evidence: Fulton measured a 5 cm fine, yellow-brown bed at 250 cm in peat, beneath a separate 1 cm Bridge River bed at 150 cm. A date below the putative Mazama is anomalously young. The stratigraphic reading gives a conditional 5 cm envelope; an identity-omission refit excludes it.

G1989-KOBAU.evidence: The field investigator reports a 10 cm bed directly below the sampled peat. This establishes the surviving thickness. Complete local retention is required to transfer its envelope to original airborne ash.

H1973-CALGARY.evidence: A continuous 5 cm band at 1.5 m below surface can be followed across roughly 8 m of exposure. Harrison interprets deposition in standing water within a dominantly colluvial section. Distinguish the enclosing paleosol and other Calgary sites. A tentative correlation and basin transfer support a ceiling.

F2018-ELSMITH.evidence: At the one registered sounding, the field report places a patchy Mazama marker between approximate 250 and 350 cm nonash occupation material. The gross ~100 cm section is a weak conditional outer bound. Other nearby patches have no registered whole-bed contacts. The reported burial depth of about 270 cm is not thickness.

B2020-133.evidence: S1 describes wash into the bog. Buckland codes the 165 cm package B (mixed). The older Glacier Peak horizon in the same cited profile bottoms at 3.45 m. From surface to that older horizon the complete core column gives a conditional ≤345 cm. The two publications share the 1992 observations; neither establishes 165 cm of original airfall.
B2020-133.assumption: Same auger station, younger Mazama above the dated couplet, and the complete local fall retained within the surface-to-marker column. Redistribution and noncapture can invalidate the inferred ceiling.

B2020-136.evidence: S1 describes a silty layer at 75 cm burial depth. Buckland codes the 65 cm package B (mixed). The older Glacier Peak horizon in the same cited profile bottoms at 2.1 m. From surface to that older horizon the complete core column gives a conditional ≤210 cm. The two publications share the 1992 observations; neither establishes 65 cm of original airfall.
B2020-136.assumption: Same auger station, younger Mazama above the dated couplet, and the complete local fall retained within the surface-to-marker column. Redistribution and noncapture can invalidate the inferred ceiling.
